GENERAL MANAGER
RECOMMENDATION:
RECOMMENDATION:
Authorize the General Manager to execute a sole source contract with InfoSend, Inc., to September 29, 2025,
with one option year for data processing, print, and mail services in the amount of $200,000 that may increase
annually at a rate of CPI plus 1%, not to exceed 5%.
BUDGET IMPACT:
Billing outsourcing costs are driven by volume and billing options. The more billing statements
mailed, the higher the costs. Color printing, various print formats and billing inserts also impact
costs. The FY25 operating budget includes $250,000 for billing outsourcing. In addition to
billing services, CVWD pays InfoSend for postage related costs that are a pass through to the U.S.
Postal Service. This contract saves CVWD significant postage costs because InfoSend leverages
its combined customer volume to obtain the most favorable bulk mail rate offered by the U.S.
Postal Service. The FY25 operating budget includes $620,000 for postage and annual budget
expenditures will be requested as part of this task order change.
This task order will keep costs in FY25 for both billing outsourcing and postage at or below the
FY25 operating budget. The task order limits any annual increase to 5% which will be accounted
for in subsequent operating budgets.
PROCUREMENT METHOD:
X Single or Sole Source
If other, please explain: .
BACKGROUND
The purpose of this board item is to request approval of a new sole source contract with InfoSend that would
extend the contract term an additional year, to September 29, 2025, with one option year and tie any annual
price increases to CPI plus 1%, not to exceed 5%. Billing outsourcing costs increased 10% from FY19 to FY23.

FY19 $163,574
FY20 $189,293 16%
FY21 $155,845 -18%
FY22 $187,506 20%
FY23 $180,069 -4%
Approval of the contract will continue CVWD’s partnership with InfoSend. InfoSend has been a District vendor for
16 years and has provided excellent service during this time. InfoSend was initially awarded a three-year
contract in 2007. In 2011, InfoSend was awarded a second contract following a competitive bid process. In
August 2014, the Board approved a three-year sole source contract with InfoSend with the option for two
additional one-year extensions. In July 2019, the Board approved a five-year sole source contract with Infosend.
The current sole source contract with InfoSend will expire September 29, 2024.
This agreement would ensure that District billing statements continue to be produced and mailed in an efficient
and cost-effective manner. A sole source contract is justified due to the following factors:
• InfoSend is highly integrated with CVWD’s billing system. Billing data is transmitted daily through a series of
data exchanges established between InfoSend, Central Square and Paymentus. Information Systems and
Customer Billing have devoted considerable time and effort to develop the billing process to ensure that data is
transferred to InfoSend efficiently, accurately, and securely. Changing vendors to a new billing company may
potentially introduce technical challenges that could impact the District’s ratepayers.
• Requesting new competitive bids at this time rather than renewing this contract would result in potential risk to
the District. The District is implementing a new ERP and UB system in the next two years, programming and
implementation costs could result in significantly higher overall costs and staff time when this time should be
dedicated to the implementation of the new software.
• InfoSend, through a partnership with our payment processing vendor Paymentus, provides an integrated
electronic bill archive. Changing vendors would result in programming cost by Paymentus or the loss of this
functionality.
• InfoSend provides customized programming to our bills including the shadow bills produced prior to rate
adjustments, delinquency postings on bills, and creation of the drought penalties.
• Data exchanges set-up through InfoSend automatically update customer addresses in CVWD’s billing system
based on the National Change of Address Database (NCOA).

RECOMMENDATION:
RECOMMENDATION:
Authorize the General Manager to execute Purchase Agreements with Northern Digital, Inc. (NDI) and Integrated
Power System (IPS) in the amounts of $325,709 and $377,228, respectively, for Programmable Logic Controller
(PLC) Panels for the PLC Upgrade Project, Phase III (Project). This authorization also includes the execution of a
Professional Services Agreement (PSA) with NDI for Professional Consulting Services in the amount of $273,920
and approve additional contingency expenditures of $33,123, for a total requested authorization of $1,010,000.
BUDGET IMPACT:
Funding for the Project is included in the Fiscal Year 2025 (FY25) Operating Budget (Budget) in the amount of
$510,000 and the Capital Improvement Budget (CIB) under the PLC Upgrade and Enhancements (GD2501) in the
amount of $500,000, for total proposed funding of $1,010,000. As such, there will be no adverse impact to FY25
Budget.

If other, please explain: .
BACKGROUND
The PLC Upgrade Program is a layered multi-year plan which includes the replacement of antiquated
instrumentation with upgraded programmable logic controllers that will provide significantly more data from our
individual sites through our Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. The upgrades will provide
for extensive cost savings and operational optimization over the next decade.
PLC Panels:
Phase III PLC Panels
Consists of the procurement of 50 Domestic PLC panels to upgrade legacy micro-Remote Terminal Units (mRTU).
The Project encompasses upgrades to the instrumentation equipment at 24 booster stations, 14 well sites, 6
reservoirs, and 6 pressure reducing stations, including 4 booster/reservoir combination sites. The upgrades will
provide for significant operational optimization through streamlined communications with our newly implemented
SCADA system.
Invitation for Bid (Bid) No. 2024-34 was advertised on July 31, 2024, and on August 28, 2024, four bids were
received. CVWD staff evaluated the bids received and selected NDI and IPS to provide 20 PLC panels and 30
PLC panels, respectively, based on the schedules below. The draft purchase agreements, Register of Bids, and
Bid details are attached.
IPS was the low bidder, and NDI was the second lowest bidder. NDI submitted a protest to the low bid in regard
to a certification requirement and the location of IPS’s facility to CVWD’s main office.
Section 6.0 of the Request for Bid (“RFB”) provides that CVWD reserves the right to waive any discrepancy or
technicality and to split or make the award in any manner determined to be most advantageous to CVWD. In
addition, Section 12.0 of the RFB provides that CVWD’s Procurement and Contracts Manager or other designated
staff will provide a decision to the protestor.
Procurement determined that it is in CVWD’s best interest to split the award between the two lowest bidders to
maximize the number of panels that could be purchased with the project budget. Procurement also determined
that the technicalities raised in the protest are immaterial and responded as such to NDI by indicating CVWD’s
right to waive minor discrepancies or technicalities. As further explained to the protestor, Procurement has
determined that the certification and location issues raised by RFB are not actually pertinent to the purchase.
Having addressed the protest at Staff level, it is recommended that CVWD proceed to split the award between
NDI and IPS to maximize the number of panels that can be purchased with the project budget.
Programming Consulting Services:
Automated Demand Response (ADR) SCADA Project
The SCADA programming required to update 22 domestic ADR sites from existing legacy mRTU's to new PLC’s.
The SCADA integration of these sites aligns with our Project.
Generator Run Time
SCADA programming required to calculate statistical generator run time data. This will differentiate maintenance
run time from Emergency Power run time to ensure compliance by South Coast Air Quality Management District.
Time of Use (TOU) SCADA Project
The TOU SCADA programming will optimize CVWD’s Domestic pumps by limiting on-peak run time which will
result in significant electrical cost savings.
Selecting NDI as a single/sole source provider ensures consistency with SCADA System implementation and its
system design standards while enhancing usability and navigation and reducing overall costs. The NDI quotes
and Single/Sole Source Justification form are attached.

The overall Project consists of three projects designed to enhance CVWD’s SCADA system to support

the domestic water system.
Project 1: Sodium Hypochlorite Conversion:
This project supports the conversion of ten domestic well sites from calcium hypochlorite tablet feeders to
sodium hypochlorite disinfection systems. SCADA modifications will provide monitoring, control, and alarm
functionality for the new equipment. Without these changes, staff will have limited visibility and operational
control of the upgraded systems. Long-term benefits include improved reliability, operational efficiency,
disinfection process control, and standardized well site operations.
Project 2: Reservoir Top-off Program Enhancements:
This project enhances the Reservoir Top-off Program (RTOP) control by improving pump selection logic and
ensuring only pumps available for automatic operation are selected. These modifications are needed to improve
the accuracy and reliability of automated pumping operations. Without the enhancements, the system may
continue to select pumps inefficiently or attempt to operate pumps that are unavailable. Long-term benefits
include improved automation performance, reduced operator intervention, and more efficient pumping
operations.
Project 3: Time-of-Use Enhancements:
This project enhances the existing AVEVA Time-of-Use (TOU) functionality to support IID's updated seasonal
TOU requirements. The modifications will automate seasonal operating schedules and improve the ability to shift
pumping operations to lower-cost energy periods. Without these enhancements, staff’s ability to fully implement
its energy management strategy is limited. Long-term benefits include reduced electrical operating costs,
improved energy efficiency, and greater operational flexibility.

As part of this implementation, communication will be established between the Oasis Reservoir PLC and

DESCRIPTION OF WORK
HMI and PLC support should include (at a minimum) the following Scope of Work and Functionality:
1. The MP 97.1 PLC will be used to initiate the Communication Requests to the Oasis PLC and
request the status of the two existing Basin High Water Switches, as well as the East and West
Basin Levels and associated High Water Setpoints from SCADA. It will also report a Link Fail
when there are communication issues between the two PLCs.
2. These two High Water Alarms will require Debounce Timers and will provide the option for
Latching Alarms that require a reset to be cleared from the Alarm Page.
3. These two High Water Alarms will have an Alarm Severity of 1.
4. An Oasis Basin Email Alert Object will need to be created in AVEVA so that Alarm Tags and
Stakeholder Email Addresses can be added in the future. Initially, it will consist of the Auto
Adjustment Event Tag, associated alarm conditions, and stakeholder email addresses.
5. When either a High Water Switch becomes active or a Basin Level meets or exceeds its
configured High Water Setpoint, the 97.1 Lateral will initiate a Timeset Closure. This will also latch
in an Auto Close Disable Bit in the PLC. This will cause a Warning Message to display on the HMI
that says, “MP 97.1 Lateral has Auto Adjusted due to Basin High Water Conditions”. It will also
generate an alarm on the alarm page. This will also have an Alarm Severity of 1. The Alarm should
read “MP 97.1 Lateral Gate Auto Adjustment Initiated. Reset after High Level Normalizes.”
6. The PLC will evaluate both discrete High Water Switch inputs and analog Basin Level values
against configurable High Water Setpoints. If a Basin Level transmitter is determined to be invalid
(e.g., range alarm), that input will be excluded from level-based evaluation, while High Water
Switches will continue to provide failsafe protection.
7. The program will not automatically close it again until both of the High Water Alarms are cleared
and Personnel resets the Alarms. Also, for a failsafe against a problem causing the High Water
inputs to chatter, a Lateral Auto Adjustment Reset will be added to the MP 97.1 Lateral Control
Options. This will not stop a user from being able to control the Lateral manually but will keep the
Auto Adjustment from initiating again following a hardware issue. When Staff/Personnel are
confident that the High Water was valid and the situation has been resolved, they can select the
MP 97.1 Lateral Control and choose the Auto Adjustment Reset. This will also clear the Auto
Adjustment Message on the HMI and the Auto Adjustment Alarm on the alarm page.
8. Even if the High Water Alarms come in and out, the automatic closure will not initiate if one of
these High Water Alarms hasn’t been Reset or if the Auto Close Disable Bit is still active.

BACKGROUND
The Mid-valley Pump Station (MVPS) is a critical facility designed to provide direct canal water, or a blend with

second (CFS). The configuration ensures operational reliability and redundancy, enabling consistent service

structure is essential, given that the full scope of repair and rebuilding costs cannot be accurately determined
until the pump is pulled from service and undergoes a complete disassembly and internal inspection. By utilizing
a rotating list, CVWD maintains a diverse pool of specialized contractors who are readily available to address
these unpredictable mechanical failures, preventing CVWD’s reliance on a single source. This approach ensures
that as hidden defects are uncovered during the inspection, CVWD can ensure expert diagnostics from
prequalified vendors to restore operational availability while adhering to municipal best practices for equitable
work distribution. The Rockwell quote and Repair Rotating Vendor List are attached; however, a contract is being

pump utilization. As a trusted integration partner, NDI remains committed to delivering robust, future-

InfoSend reserves the right to increase InfoSend Fees on an annual basis starting with the first anniversary of the Effective Date to

THIS AGREEMENT FOR CONTRACT SERVICES (“Agreement”) is made and entered

sole source contract due to the fact that these services are highly integrated with the current billing
system.
D. CVWD desires to retain the services of Contractor for the Data Processing, Print
and Mail Services.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the promises and mutual obligations, covenants,
and conditions contained herein, and other valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of
which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
AGREEMENT
1. CONTRACTOR SERVICES
1.1 Scope of Services. In compliance with all terms and conditions of this Agreement,
Contractor shall provide services to CVWD as described in the Scope of Services/Work attached
to this Agreement as Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by reference (the “Services” or “Work”).
Exhibit "A" includes the agreed upon schedule of performance and the schedule of fees.
Contractor warrants that the Services shall be performed in a competent, professional, and
satisfactory manner consistent with the level of care and skill ordinarily exercised by high quality,
experienced, and well qualified members of the profession currently practicing under similar
conditions. In the event of any inconsistency between the terms contained in the Scope of
Services/Work and the terms set forth in this Agreement, the terms set forth in this Agreement
shall govern.
1.2 Compliance with Law. Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state,
and local laws, statutes and ordinances and all lawful orders, rules, and regulations when
performing the Services. Contractor shall be liable for all violations of such laws and regulations
in connection with the Services and this Agreement.

delay.

3.1 Compensation of Contractor. Contractor shall be compensated and reimbursed
for the services rendered under this Agreement in accordance with the schedule of fees set forth
in Exhibit “B”. The total amount of Compensation shall not exceed $2,610,000, including an

payment, Contractor shall submit to the District an invoice for Services rendered prior to the date

finance director. Payments shall be based on the schedule of fees set forth in Exhibit “B” for
authorized services performed. The District shall pay Contractor for all expenses stated in the
invoice that are approved by the District and consistent with this Agreement, within thirty (30) days
of receipt of Contractor’s invoice.

District, Parties shall execute a written amendment to this Agreement, specifying all proposed
amendments, including, but not limited to, any additional fees. An amendment may be entered
into:
A. To provide for revisions or modifications to documents, work product, or
Work, when required by the enactment or revision of any subsequent law; or
B. To provide for additional services not included in this Agreement or not
customarily furnished in accordance with generally accepted practice in Contractor’s profession.
3.4 Appropriations. This Agreement is subject to, and contingent upon, funds being
appropriated by CVWD for each fiscal year. If such appropriations are not made, this Agreement
shall automatically terminate without penalty to the District.

performed under the agreed upon schedule of performance set forth in Exhibit “A.” Any time
period extension must be approved in writing by the Contract Officer.
4.3 Force Majeure. The time for performance of Services to be rendered under this
Agreement may be extended because of any delays due to a Force Majeure Event if Contractor
